01 / Spare-time volunteering · Community event

Helping kids start painting
with confidence.

I volunteered and helped organize this community event in my spare time.

Printed bilingual boards for the craft table. Simple subjects, bright colors, and an open invitation to draw anything they love.

The challenge I identified through proactive pre-testing

By proactively pre-testing craft activities ahead of a large community event, I realized that children might pick up a blank kite and not know what to do or where to start. I wanted to give them a clear, welcoming starting point.

The choices I made

I chose familiar subjects and directed the artwork to feel appealing and achievable. English and Chinese text welcomed families into the activity. The final line left the choice with each child: draw anything you love.

A little inspiration.
Enough confidence to begin.

Result

At the event, kids looked at the boards, chose what to paint, and got started happily.

Event context: 100+ people from 60+ families.

How the boards were made

I photographed real objects, used AI to render the imagery under my art direction, and typeset the bilingual boards. I printed the finished designs for the station.

02 / Painting for myself & friends

Sometimes, the right tool
is a paintbrush.

A name sign for a friend’s newborn. A quiet figure in warm colors. Painting is another way I pay attention — to the person, the feeling, and the details that make something worth keeping.

Every Thursday: what's claimable, what's still being watched, and anything that needs you — nothing more.

Rendered from Price Droper's real templates, with example orders and anonymized brand names — no real order data.

The everyday problem

A purchase goes on sale after you buy it. Getting a price adjustment means remembering to check, finding the policy, and figuring out what to say.

The choices I made

An email is the interface. The amount appears first, the deadline stays close, and a prepared message makes the next step easier. A weekly report keeps the rest together.

The useful part isn’t just
“the price dropped.”
It’s “here’s what to do next.”

Care in the details

Match the exact size and color. Check the adjustment window. Send alerts when there is something to act on. Each choice removes a little work for the person receiving it.

Current scope: Automated daily checks and AI-assisted monitoring for my go-to everyday brands.

I like making everyday life
a little easier.
And a little more lovely.

A starting point for a child. A clear next step for a shopper. A gift made for one particular person. Different materials, the same attention to who it’s for.
